name: radiology-research
title: Radiology order text (research pack)
description: Research and education pack. Reads the text of imaging orders and shows the lines that match rules written from public guidelines. Synthetic data only; not for patient care.
banner: Research and education software. Not a medical device; not cleared, approved or CE-marked. Not for patient care, including choosing which studies to read first. It reads only text, quotes the exact words that matched a rule, and never changes the ordered priority. Accuracy figures come from synthetic cases. Clinical use may be regulated as a medical device.

tiers.name: Discuss now
tiers.description: The text matches a rule for a condition where imaging within minutes to about an hour can change what happens next.

tiers.name: Today
tiers.description: The text matches a rule for a condition usually imaged and read the same day.

tiers.name: In order
tiers.description: Baseline. Shown under 'No rule matched' in the original order.

onset.label: Symptom onset or last known well
patterns: (?:last known well|last seen (?:well|normal)|last known normal|\bLKW|\bLSW|symptom onset|onset(?: time)?)\s*(?:at|@|was|:|=|~|approx\.?|about|around)?\s*(?<time>\d{1,2}[:.]\d{2}\s*(?:am|pm)?|[0-2]\d[0-5]\d(?![\d/])|\d{1,2}\s*(?:am|pm))

source.citation: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke

rules.title: Possible acute stroke
rules.why: New one-sided weakness, facial droop, speech loss or half-field vision loss can mean acute stroke. Treatment windows count from last known well: thrombolysis within 4.5 hours, thrombectomy up to 24 hours for selected patients.

source.citation: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke

rules.title: Possible intracranial bleed
rules.why: A sudden severe ('thunderclap', 'worst ever') headache or a suspected bleed needs an immediate non-contrast CT head; on anticoagulants, a drop in consciousness or new confusion raises the same question.

source.citation: NICE NG228 Subarachnoid haemorrhage caused by a ruptured aneurysm: diagnosis and management

rules.title: Head injury with a high-risk feature
rules.why: After a head injury, GCS below 15, signs of skull fracture, a seizure, a focal deficit or more than one vomit are reasons for CT head within 1 hour.

source.citation: NICE NG232 Head injury: assessment and early management

rules.title: GCS 12 or less
rules.why: A Glasgow Coma Scale of 12 or less is the NICE head-injury threshold for CT within 1 hour. This pack applies the same threshold to any request that states it.

source.citation: NICE NG232 Head injury: assessment and early management

rules.title: Possible cauda equina syndrome
rules.why: Back pain or sciatica with saddle numbness, new bladder or bowel change, or symptoms in both legs: the national pathway asks for an emergency MRI within 4 hours of the request reaching radiology.

source.citation: GIRFT National Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome Pathway (2023, revised 2026)

rules.title: Possible spinal cord compression
rules.why: Known or suspected cancer with new back pain and leg weakness, a sensory level or sphincter change: MRI as soon as possible and always within 24 hours.

source.citation: NICE NG234 Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression

rules.title: Possible spinal epidural abscess
rules.why: Back pain with fever and a risk factor (injecting drug use, a recent spinal procedure, bacteraemia) needs urgent contrast MRI; any suspicion warrants immediate evaluation.

source.citation: StatPearls: Spinal Epidural Abscess (NCBI Bookshelf)

rules.title: Possible pulmonary embolism
rules.why: Suspected acute pulmonary embolism, or pleuritic pain or breathlessness with a fast heart rate, low saturation or a clot risk factor: CT pulmonary angiography is the first-line test when probability is high.

source.citation: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism

rules.title: Possible aortic dissection
rules.why: Sudden tearing chest or back pain, a blood pressure difference between arms or a stated suspicion of dissection: contrast CT of the aorta as early as possible.

source.citation: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of peripheral arterial and aortic diseases

rules.title: Possible ruptured or leaking aortic aneurysm
rules.why: A known or palpable aneurysm with collapse, low blood pressure or new abdominal, back or flank pain, or a stated suspicion of rupture: prompt CT angiography.

source.citation: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms

rules.title: Possible pneumothorax
rules.why: A suspected pneumothorax, especially after a procedure, with breathlessness or with signs of tension, sits on critical-result lists and needs a prompt film.

source.citation: British Thoracic Society Guideline for pleural disease (Thorax 2023)

rules.title: Possible perforation or anastomotic leak
rules.why: Suspected free air, a perforated viscus, an anastomotic leak or generalised peritonism: CT is the recommended test for an acute abdomen with suspected perforation.

source.citation: WSES guidelines: Perforated and bleeding peptic ulcer (World J Emerg Surg 2020)

rules.title: Possible acute mesenteric ischaemia
rules.why: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to a soft abdomen, especially with atrial fibrillation, vascular disease or a raised lactate: CT angiography without delay.

source.citation: Acute mesenteric ischemia: updated guidelines of the World Society of Emergency Surgery (2022)

rules.title: Possible testicular or ovarian torsion
rules.why: Sudden testicular pain, or sudden one-sided pelvic pain with a known cyst or enlarged ovary, can mean torsion: an emergency where imaging must not delay surgical assessment.

source.citation: EAU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology, Acute Scrotum (2026); ACOG Committee Opinion 783 Adnexal Torsion in Adolescents (2019)

rules.title: Possible ectopic pregnancy
rules.why: A positive pregnancy test with pain, bleeding or collapse and no confirmed intrauterine pregnancy, or a stated suspicion of ectopic pregnancy.

source.citation: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management

rules.title: Possible malrotation, volvulus or intussusception
rules.why: Bilious (green) vomiting in a baby suggests malrotation with volvulus; episodic screaming with drawn-up legs or redcurrant jelly stool suggests intussusception.

source.citation: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Vomiting in Infants (2020) and Abdominal Pain-Child (2025)

rules.title: Suspected inflicted injury with neurological change
rules.why: Every infant under 1 with suspected physical abuse gets a CT head as well as a skeletal survey; with drowsiness, seizures, apnoea, vomiting or a bulging fontanelle this pack treats it as time-critical.

source.citation: RCR and RCPCH: The radiological investigation of suspected physical abuse in children

rules.title: Button battery, magnets or airway foreign body
rules.why: A swallowed button battery can burn the oesophagus within about 2 hours and must be located on X-ray at once; several magnets and an inhaled foreign body with breathing symptoms are also time-critical.

source.citation: National Capital Poison Center: Button Battery Ingestion Triage and Treatment Guideline

rules.title: Possible necrotising soft tissue infection
rules.why: Pain out of proportion, rapidly spreading redness, crepitus, bullae or skin colour change in a soft tissue infection: prompt surgical consultation; imaging must not delay it.

source.citation: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: 2014 Update

rules.title: Possible obstructed and infected kidney
rules.why: A kidney stone or hydronephrosis with fever or sepsis, or obstruction of a single kidney, is an emergency that needs urgent decompression.

source.citation: EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis (2026)

rules.title: Signs of shock in the request
rules.why: Systolic blood pressure of 90 or less, a heart rate above 130 or a stated instability puts the scan on a resuscitation pathway. This pack borrows the sepsis high-risk thresholds.

source.citation: NICE NG253 Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management

rules.title: Active or massive bleeding
rules.why: Massive haemoptysis, haematemesis or other active bleeding with instability needs imaging or intervention as part of resuscitation.

source.citation: NICE CG141 Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management

rules.title: Possible acute limb ischaemia
rules.why: A cold, pale, pulseless or numb limb of sudden onset threatens the limb within hours.

source.citation: ESVS 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Acute Limb Ischaemia

rules.title: Transient neurological symptoms
rules.why: Neurological symptoms that have fully resolved (possible TIA) need prompt specialist assessment and imaging, not a thrombolysis pathway.

source.citation: NICE NG128 Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management

rules.title: Head injury on anticoagulants
rules.why: A head injury in someone taking anticoagulants: NICE advises considering CT within 8 hours of the injury even without other features.

source.citation: NICE NG232 Head injury: assessment and early management

rules.title: Low oxygen saturation
rules.why: A stated saturation below 92% is below the usual 94 to 98% target range for acutely ill adults. The 92% threshold is this pack's own choice.

source.citation: BTS Guideline for oxygen use in healthcare and emergency settings (2017)

rules.title: Possible appendicitis
rules.why: Right lower quadrant pain or a stated suspicion of appendicitis is usually imaged the same day.

source.citation: WSES Jerusalem guidelines on diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020)

rules.title: Possible bowel obstruction
rules.why: Absolute constipation, distension with vomiting or a stated suspicion of obstruction is usually imaged the same day.

source.citation: Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction, 2017 update

rules.title: Possible cholecystitis or cholangitis
rules.why: Right upper quadrant pain with fever, a positive Murphy's sign or jaundice with fever is usually imaged the same day.

source.citation: Tokyo Guidelines 2018: diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis

rules.title: Possible deep vein thrombosis
rules.why: If DVT is likely, NICE asks for a proximal leg vein ultrasound result within 4 hours (or within 24 hours with interim anticoagulation).

source.citation: NICE NG158 Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing

rules.title: Possible kidney stone
rules.why: Renal colic without fever is usually imaged the same day; fever or a single kidney moves it to the obstructed-infected-kidney rule.

source.citation: EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis (2026)

rules.title: Possible abscess, collection or deep infection
rules.why: A suspected abscess, collection, septic joint, bone or disc infection is usually imaged the same day to plan drainage or treatment.

source.citation: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: 2014 Update

rules.title: Possible fracture needing same-day imaging
rules.why: A suspected hip or other fracture where imaging decides same-day management.

source.citation: NICE CG124 Hip fracture: management

rules.title: Suspected inflicted injury
rules.why: A suspected non-accidental injury in a child needs a same-day imaging plan (skeletal survey, CT head in infants).

source.citation: RCR and RCPCH: The radiological investigation of suspected physical abuse in children

rules.title: First seizure or signs of raised intracranial pressure
rules.why: This pack treats a new first seizure, or worsening headache with vomiting, as same-day. NICE NG217 asks for urgent specialist referral after a first seizure and sets no emergency imaging rule, so the same-day choice is this pack's own.

source.citation: NICE NG217 Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

rules.title: Tube or line position check
rules.why: A nasogastric tube must be confirmed in the stomach before anything is put down it; position checks should not wait in the normal order.

source.citation: NHS Improvement (2016): Nasogastric tube misplacement: continuing risk of death and severe harm (NHS/PSA/RE/2016/006)

rules.title: Possible pyloric stenosis
rules.why: Projectile, non-bilious vomiting in a young infant suggests pyloric stenosis, which is usually imaged the same day.

source.citation: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Vomiting in Infants (2020)
